m: Salutation to Shri Ganesha. Of these three secrets of the Shri Saptashati, the seers are Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra, the deities are Mahakali, Mahalakshmi, and Mahasarasvati, the metre is anushtubh, the seed is Navadurga and Mahalakshmi, and the power is Shrim. This direction is for recitation so that the fruit I desire may succeed. The king said: Blessed one, you have told me the descents of Chandika. You should tell, O knower of Brahman, the primal nature of these.
Tell me fully and properly, twice-born one, since I have bowed, the form of the Goddess that is to be worshipped by me, and the manner of it.
The seer said: This is called the supreme secret, not to be told. Because you are a devotee, lord of men, there is nothing I should withhold from you.
Mahalakshmi is the first of all, the supreme sovereign of the three qualities. Her form is both what can be marked and what cannot, and she remains, pervading the whole.
She bears a citron, a mace, a shield, and a drinking-cup, and on her head, O king, she bears a serpent, a linga, and a yoni.
Her colour is like heated gold, and her ornaments are of heated gold. She filled all that void with her own splendour.
Seeing that the whole world was void, the supreme sovereign took another form, by tamas alone.
She, resembling a streak of collyrium, her excellent face set with fangs, a woman with wide eyes, became slender-waisted.
Her four arms were adorned with sword, cup, head, and shield. On her head she wore a garland of headless trunks and a garland of serpents' heads.
Mahalakshmi said to her, that excellent woman of tamas: I give you names. Those are your works.
Mahamaya, Mahakali, Mahamari, hunger, thirst, sleep, craving, Ekavira, Kalaratri, hard to pass beyond.
These names of yours are to be set forth by the works. Knowing the works by these, the one who recites obtains happiness.
Having said this to her, Mahalakshmi, O king, took another form by the very pure quality called sattva, a form bright as the moon.
Bearing a rosary and a goad, holding a vina and a book, she became an excellent woman, and Mahalakshmi gave her names.
Mahavidya, Mahavani, Bharati, speech, Sarasvati, Arya, Brahmi, Kamadhenu, womb of the Veda, sovereign of the gods.
Then Mahalakshmi said to Mahakali and to Sarasvati: You two goddesses, bring forth a pair, each according to her own form.
Having said this to them, Mahalakshmi herself created a pair, a beautiful woman and man, golden-wombed, seated on a lotus.
She called that man Brahman, Vidhi, Virinchi, and Dhata. The mother called that woman Shri, Padma, Kamala, and Lakshmi.
Mahakali and Bharati together bring forth a pair. I will tell you the forms and the names of these two as well.
Mahakali brought forth a man with a dark throat, red arms, a white body, and the moon on his crest, and a white woman.
He is Rudra, Shankara, Sthanu, Kapardi, and the three-eyed. That woman is the knowledge of the three, Kamadhenu, language, the svaras, and the syllables.
Sarasvati, O king, brought forth a woman, Gauri, and a man, Krishna. I will tell you their names as well.
He is Vishnu, Krishna, Hrishikesha, Vasudeva, Janardana. She is Uma, Gauri, Sati, Chandi, Sundari, Subhaga, Shubha.
Thus the young women at once attained the state of persons. Those who have eyes see this. Other people, who do not know it, do not.
Mahalakshmi gave Brahma a wife, the three Vedas, O king. She gave Rudra Gauri, the giver of boons, and she gave Vasudeva Shri.
Joining with the woman of speech, Virinchi generated the egg. The blessed Rudra, together with that Gauri, valiant, split it.
Inside the egg, O king, there arose the host of effects, beginning with primal matter: the whole world, whose self is the great elements, what stands still and what moves.
Keshava, together with that Lakshmi, nourished it and protected it. Mahalakshmi is thus unborn, O king, sovereign of all sovereigns.

She is without form and with form, and she herself bears many names. She is to be discerned by those names, and by no other name. Thus the secret of the primal one, in the Devi Mahatmya of the Savarnika manvantara in the Markandeya Purana, is complete.
